content.user_title: Create implementation plans for code changes
content.value_statement: Large code changes fail when requirements, files, and validation steps are unclear. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to produce structured implementation plans before work starts.
actual_capabilities: Creates .todo.md plan documents inside a .plans directory.
Maps original requirements to specific implementation steps.
Provides separate guidance for feature, refactor, and fix plans.
Prompts review of CLAUDE.md files and existing code patterns.
Includes impact analysis, removal specification, anti-patterns, and validation criteria.
limitations: It does not implement the planned code changes.
It depends on the available issue text and repository context.
GitHub issue extraction may require the GitHub CLI and repository access.
Its strict no-migration guidance may need adjustment for public APIs.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Feature
use_cases.description: A product engineer converts a feature request into a scoped implementation plan with requirements and validation steps.

use_cases.title: Structure a Refactor
use_cases.description: A tech lead documents affected files, reused types, removal steps, and quality checks before changing shared code.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Bug Fix
use_cases.description: A maintainer captures root cause, affected paths, safeguards, and regression tests before fixing a defect.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a plan for this task: [paste task]. Include summary, affected files, implementation steps, and validation checks.

prompt_templates.title: Plan from GitHub Issue
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a .plans implementation plan for issue [number]. Extract every requirement and map each requirement to plan steps.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Refactor
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a refactor plan for [area]. Review existing patterns, identify reusable types, list removals, and define validation criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Complex Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a complete implementation plan from this analysis: [paste analysis]. Include impact, risks, dependencies, removal specification, and test coverage.

output_examples.input: A request to add user notification preferences.
output_examples.output: A plan title, requirements table, affected settings files, implementation steps, removal notes, and validation checks for preference updates.

output_examples.input: A bug report about failed password reset emails.
output_examples.output: A fix plan describing root cause investigation, mailer changes, regression tests, and acceptance criteria for successful reset delivery.

output_examples.input: A refactor request for duplicated billing logic.
output_examples.output: A refactor plan listing shared billing modules, dependencies to update, old code to remove, and behavior checks.

best_practices: Provide the original issue or analysis before invoking the skill.
Let the model inspect related files and local instructions before drafting the plan.
Review the plan for external API compatibility before implementation.
anti_patterns: Using the skill when you only need a small direct edit.
Skipping requirement extraction and asking for a plan from vague context.
Treating the generated plan as approval to change code without review.

faq.question: Does this skill write code?
faq.answer: No. It creates implementation plans that guide later code changes.

faq.question: Where does it place plans?
faq.answer: It instructs the assistant to create .todo.md files in a .plans directory.

faq.question: Can it plan bug fixes?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a fix template with root cause, safeguards, and regression tests.

faq.question: Can it use GitHub issues?
faq.answer: Yes, when the GitHub CLI and repository access are available.

faq.question: Does it support Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: What should users review before implementation?
faq.answer: Check requirement coverage, affected files, validation steps, and any compatibility needs.
